# Temple Scroll Column 59 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 59 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 59:2 — "pass through the fire" vs. "sacrifice in the fire"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "makes his son or daughter pass through the fire" | Literal ma'avir — the standard Hebrew expression for Molech worship |
| LOGOS | "makes his son or daughter pass through fire" | Same rendering, standard |
| PNEUMA | "sacrifice a son or daughter in the fire" | Interprets the ritual as child sacrifice |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "makes his son or daughter pass through fire" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hebrew phrase should be preserved; whether this always involved lethal sacrifice is debated. Translation should not predetermine the interpretation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 59:3-4 — divination vocabulary

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "diviner of divinations, soothsayer, augur, sorcerer, charmer of charms, one who inquires of a spirit, knowing-one, one who seeks to the dead" | Literal Hebrew terms with etymological compounds |
| LOGOS | "divination, soothsayer, augur, sorcerer, charmer, medium, wizard, necromancer" | Standard scholarly English equivalents |
| PNEUMA | "fortune-telling, interpret omens, cast spells, charms, spirit medium, communicate with the dead" | Modern equivalents for accessibility |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS catalogue. The standard English terms (medium, wizard, necromancer) are well established in biblical translation and scholarship. EMET's compounds are unwieldy; PNEUMA's modernizations lose the technical specificity.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 59:6 — "whole" vs. "blameless" vs. "completely faithful"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "whole you shall be" | Literal tamim — "complete, whole, perfect" |
| LOGOS | "blameless" | Standard rendering in English Bibles (cf. Gen 17:1) |
| PNEUMA | "completely faithful" | Interpretive expansion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "blameless" (LOGOS). This is the standard rendering of tamim in covenantal contexts. EMET's "whole" is ambiguous in English; PNEUMA's "completely faithful" adds "faithful" beyond the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 59:9 — "require it from him" vs. "hold him accountable" vs. "personally hold accountable"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I will require it from him" | Literal 'anokhi edrosh me'immo — God will seek/demand from him |
| LOGOS | "I Myself will hold him accountable" | Emphatic divine first person with modern legal accountability language |
| PNEUMA | "I will personally hold that person accountable" | Same, with additional emphasis |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "I Myself will hold him accountable" (LOGOS). The emphatic pronoun is important; "require" (EMET) is unclear in modern English. PNEUMA's "personally" is redundant with "I Myself."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 59:18 — "redeemer of blood" vs. "avenger of blood" vs. "dead man's relative"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "redeemer of blood" | Literal go'el ha-dam — from the root g-'-l "to redeem" |
| LOGOS | "avenger of blood" | Standard English rendering in biblical scholarship |
| PNEUMA | "the dead man's relative who wants revenge" | Explanatory paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "avenger of blood" (LOGOS). This is the universally recognized rendering. EMET's "redeemer" imports redemption theology inappropriate here; PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the technical legal term.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 59:17 — "iron slips from the wood" vs. "iron head slips from the handle"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the iron slips from the wood" | Literal — "iron" for axe head, "wood" for handle |
| LOGOS | "the iron head slips from the handle" | Clarifying additions for comprehension |
| PNEUMA | "the axe head flies off the handle" | Vivid modern language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The clarifying "head" and "handle" are necessary for English comprehension without departing from the Hebrew sense. PNEUMA's "flies off" is too vivid and adds force not in the original.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
